illustrations.position_quote: Fractions, decimals, and percentages are three ways to represent the same quantities.
illustrations.description: A three-node conversion map linking fraction, decimal, and percentage, with arrows labeled fraction to decimal: divide numerator by denominator; decimal to percent: multiply by 100; percent to decimal: divide by 100.
illustrations.why: It would make the relationships among the three representations visible at a glance and help students choose the correct conversion direction.

illustrations.position_quote: A retail store applies a $20\%$ discount on a jacket. During a clearance sale, an additional $25\%$ discount is applied to the discounted price. What is the total equivalent percentage discount from the original price?
illustrations.description: A 100-unit bar shrinking to 80 units after the first discount, then to 60 units after the second discount, with each percentage labeled against its current base.
illustrations.why: It would show why successive discounts use different base amounts and why the discounts cannot simply be added.
